list: the official 55 trophies, 2026-11-18 (1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze; 28 hidden on PSN until earned; no online trophies)

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum needs no task of its own: it unlocks the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned. Work the roadmap in order — story first so nothing with a window slips past, stranger strands while their givers are still around, counted activities next, collectible sweeps after that, and the 100% completion trophy last because it already demands most of the rest. If a single trophy is blocking the platinum, isolate it with the kind and grade filters in this tracker.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this unlocks in the first stretch of play and cannot be missed. Follow the mission objectives through to the completion screen instead of wandering off mid-mission. Treat it as the tutorial it is: the movement, driving and fishing basics it teaches come back later, including the fishing challenge against Cal.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: A story-progress trophy for finishing every mission in Chapter 1; the chapter cannot end any other way, so there is nothing to miss. Before pushing into Chapter 2, clear any stranger markers already on the map and sample each activity type you have unlocked — several strand givers move on as chapters advance, and one meditation trophy is reported to hinge on a Chapter 1 moment.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Story progression for completing Chapter 2, awarded automatically when the chapter's final mission ends. The name is shown exactly as PlayStation publishes it, asterisks included. Use the chapter break to finish any open stranger strands and to bank counted progress (stunts, races, challenges) while new areas open up, rather than leaving every counter for the endgame.

sources.name: Press Start — full trophy list, 18 Nov 2026

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Story progression for completing Chapter 3. Nothing here can be missed — the trophy fires when the chapter closes. By this point the map is largely open, so it is a good moment to sweep exploration and collectible trophies that need the whole state, and to check the missable early-warning list in this tracker before the story moves any strand givers on.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Story progression for completing Chapter 4, the last numbered chapter before the finale. It cannot be missed. With only the final mission ahead, finish any remaining stranger strands now — the 8-strand silver trophy needs eight completed strands, and late-story progress is exactly when givers can disappear.

sources.name: Press Start — full trophy list, 18 Nov 2026

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: One of the list's two gold trophies, for completing the final mission. It is story progression and cannot be missed, but keep a manual save before starting the finale: story missions cannot be replayed, and a pre-finale save is cheap insurance for anything tied to a story window. After the credits, free-roam cleanup (counts, collectibles, 100%) remains available for the rest of the roadmap.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the named story mission Breakfast Run. Named-mission trophies like this one unlock as the story reaches them, so simply play the mission to its end. If a mission offers a choice, note that choices feed a separate counter trophy — there is no need to chase a specific outcome for this one.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the named story mission The Cartel Heist. Play it through to the mission-complete screen; no optional objective is named in the description, so none is required for the trophy. Heist-style missions are also good practice for the standalone robbery trophies (bank vaults, armored truck, jewelry store) later in the roadmap.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the named story mission Child's Play. Like the other named-mission trophies it is pure story progression: finish the mission and it unlocks. The description names no optional condition, so do not restart for a cleaner run on this trophy's account.

sources.name: Press Start — full trophy list, 18 Nov 2026

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the named story mission Headliners. The all-caps name is PlayStation's own spelling, kept as published. Finish the mission to unlock it; the description sets no score, time or stealth condition, so a straightforward completion is enough.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the named story mission VCIA Takedown. Note the airport in the mission name: a separate trophy asks for an unscheduled departure at VCIA, so while this mission puts you at the airport, check that trophy's guide and consider banking it in the same visit if the game allows free movement there.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the named story mission Operation Savage Glory. Pure story progression like the other named missions: play it to the end. Keep a manual save before big late-story missions in general — with no mission replay, a save slot is the only way back to a story window.

sources.name: Press Start — full trophy list, 18 Nov 2026

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The second gold trophy, and the hardest on the list: reach 100% on the game's own completion tracker. Guides describe that tracker as a 35-task checklist finished after the story, with thresholds below true completion (PowerPyx puts it near 60% of everything), and several trophy targets sit under the checklist's numbers — 250 stunts for the trophy against 300 for 100%, 50 challenges against 70. Most of the percentage arrives while chasing other trophies, so leave this for last and track the percentage with the stepper here.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts — the count is in the description itself, and PlayStation tracks it, so the stepper here mirrors the PSN target. Stunts are repeatable free-roam fare: work them in batches between story missions instead of grinding all 250 at the end. Note the 100% checklist asks for 300, so stopping at 250 earns this silver but leaves 50 more for A Long Road.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every activity type once — reports put the number of types at nine, and the stepper here uses that figure. Do this early: sampling each activity as it unlocks also teaches the systems the counted trophies depend on (races, range challenges, drone races, fishing, bowling, arcade). If one type stays untried, the cited lists name the full set; the description alone does not.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn gold in every Shooting Range challenge — 42 of them, the count PlayStation tracks for this trophy. Gold on all 42 is a skill grind, not a checklist sweep: learn each challenge's scoring first, then chase golds in short sessions. Track golds with the stepper; silver and bronze medals do not advance the counter.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location — the description says 'every', and this guide deliberately states no location total, because the official text gives none. Win once per location (repeat wins at one spot do not help), and use the cited lists for the confirmed location set rather than guessing a number. Drone races are short, so clear each new location as the story opens its area.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — 'different' is the load-bearing word: repeat wins on one course count once, so spread wins across courses and use the stepper for distinct wins only. The 100% checklist asks for 30 unique race wins, ten more than this trophy, so racing past 20 is never wasted on a platinum run.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge — a single head-to-head win, not a fishing total. The opening mission teaches the fishing basics, so this is winnable early; if Cal keeps winning, return after story progress unlocks better gear or spots rather than grinding rematches. The description names no spot or fish, so follow the challenge marker in game and the cited guides for the confirmed trigger.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete any one arcade game — a single completion, not a high score. Find an arcade cabinet in free roam and play its game through to the end screen. It is one of the quickest bronzes on the list and doubles as one of the activity types for Master of None, so bank it the first time you pass an arcade.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missable_reason: The description names one person's final mission: Andy's strand must be started and finished while Andy is still available, and stranger strands are reported to have windows tied to story progress.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Andy's stranger strand — the whole strand, not just its opener. Stranger strands are the roadmap's stage 2 for a reason: reports say these chains have windows tied to story progress, so finish Andy's missions as they appear instead of saving them for free-roam cleanup. This strand also counts toward the 8-strand silver trophy.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missable_reason: The description names one person's final mission: Kenton's strand must be completed while Kenton is still available, and stranger strands are reported to have windows tied to story progress.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Kenton's stranger strand. As with every named strand, the trophy needs the strand's last mission, so work the chain in order whenever Kenton's markers appear. Stranger chains are reported to close as the story advances — treat an open strand as perishable and finish it before pushing the next chapter.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missable_reason: The description names one person's final mission: Billy's strand must be completed while Billy is still available, and stranger strands are reported to have windows tied to story progress.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Billy's stranger strand. The pattern is the same as the other named strands: the trophy fires on the last mission of the chain, and the chain counts toward the 8-strand silver. Because strand windows are reported to follow story progress, do not leave Billy half-finished across a chapter break.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.missable_reason: The description demands 8 completed stranger strands: every strand that closes unfinished makes the total harder, and stranger strands are reported to have windows tied to story progress.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida — a silver built entirely from other trophies' work: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each carry their own bronze for their final mission, so five of the eight come with trophies attached. Track completed strands with the stepper, and start every strand you meet; a strand never started cannot be finished if its window closes.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missable_reason: The description names one person's final mission: Randy's strand must be completed while Randy is still available, and stranger strands are reported to have windows tied to story progress.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Randy's stranger strand. Finish the full chain when Randy's markers appear; the last mission is the one that pays the trophy and one of the eight strands the silver trophy counts. With strand windows reported to follow the story, an unfinished Randy chain is exactly the kind of thing the early-warning list in this tracker exists for.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missable_reason: The description names one person's final mission: Tyrone's strand must be completed while Tyrone is still available, and stranger strands are reported to have windows tied to story progress.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Tyrone's stranger strand. Same rules as the other four named strands: whole chain, last mission pays, counts toward the 8-strand silver. Work it as soon as it opens — the reported link between strand windows and story progress makes 'later' the risky option.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.missable_reason: The description demands every meditation spot, and this is the one trophy GTABase and PowerPyx report as possibly missable, tied to a meditation session with Lucia in Chapter 1 — unconfirmed, but the cost of doing it early is zero.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida. Sources disagree on the total — GTABase puts the trophy at 18 spots while the published 100% checklist asks for 15 — so this tracker steps to 18 and says so plainly rather than hiding the disagreement. GTABase and PowerPyx flag this as the list's only possibly missable trophy, tied to a Chapter 1 meditation session with Lucia; unconfirmed, but do that session when it appears and sweep the remaining spots in stage 4.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.missable_reason: The description ties the hunt to one person, Bret: like the named stranger strands, a person-bound task can close when story progress moves that person on.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret — a person-bound task, so treat it like the stranger strands: take it when Bret offers it and finish it promptly. 'Unique' means the specific animal Bret wants, not any hunt; follow the task's own markers and the cited guides for the confirmed target rather than hunting at random. It sits in stage 2 with the other people-bound work.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 Collectible Card sets — sets, not single cards, so the stepper counts finished sets only. Collectibles are stage-4 work: sweep them once the whole map is open and story windows no longer matter. The description does not say which three sets, so any three completed sets satisfy it; use the cited lists for set contents and locations instead of guessing.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations — the count is in the description and matches the 100% checklist's figure, so no extra locations are owed for A Long Road. This is a sweep trophy: work it area by area in stage 4 with the stepper running, and lean on the cited lists for the location set. The name's capitalisation is PlayStation's own, kept as published.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 Challenges — a pure counter, tracked here with the stepper. Challenges overlap with normal play (driving, combat, exploration), so many complete without dedicated grinding; check the in-game challenge list periodically and mop up the near-misses. The 100% checklist asks for 70, twenty beyond this trophy, so challenges past 50 still pay off on a platinum run.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missable_reason: The description needs two conditions at once — a 4-star Wanted Level and your partner present — so it can only be attempted while partner free-roam is available; flagged so it is not left until partner access changes.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star Wanted Level with your partner along and escape the heat. Two conditions must hold together: the wanted level must actually reach four stars, and your partner must be with you while you shake it. Build the heat deliberately in an area with good escape routes, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear — losing the level, not outrunning it forever, is what the description asks for.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missable_reason: The description needs your partner present and a Wanted Level held across three robberies — a paired, chained condition that depends on partner availability, so it is flagged rather than left to chance.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level. The chain is the trophy: rob one shop, keep the wanted level alive (do not hide until it clears), and move straight to the next shop with your partner still along. Pick three shops close together beforehand so travel time cannot break the chain, and count only shops robbed inside one unbroken wanted stretch.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — distinct models encountered, tracked here with the stepper. Discovery accrues naturally while driving, stealing and browsing showrooms, so most players reach triple figures without trying; the last few usually need deliberate hunting in different districts and at different times. The cited lists name the vehicle set if a specific model is proving elusive.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies inside a single use of Combat Focus. The count is per activation, not cumulative, so set it up: engage a group of at least five, trigger Combat Focus once, and finish all five before it ends. Story shootouts with dense enemy groups are the natural venue; if a fight ends at four, reload the checkpoint rather than hoping the next fight lines up better.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missable_reason: The description pins the act to one place, VCIA: airport access and layout are story-dependent (VCIA Takedown is a named mission), so the departure window is flagged instead of assumed permanent.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — the airport named in the VCIA Takedown mission. The description gives no steps beyond the place and the act, so this guide invents none: when free movement at VCIA is available, get airborne or out by an unscheduled route and watch for the unlock, and check the cited guides for the confirmed trigger. Bank it while airport access is open rather than assuming it stays that way.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The official description — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — is a joke, not instructions: it names the Rhino tank and heat, and nothing else. This guide will not invent a location or a wanted-level recipe the text does not support. The cited lists carry the confirmed trigger; the honest summary from the description alone is that a Rhino and police heat are both involved.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — the stealth condition is the whole trophy. Approach unseen, keep witnesses from raising the alarm, and leave clean; if detection happens, break off and retry rather than finishing the robbery loud, because a loud success does not count. The description names no specific store, so any jewelry store robbery completed undetected satisfies it.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each — the escape is part of the requirement, so a vault emptied but followed by arrest or death should not be counted. Five separate successful vault robberies, tracked with the stepper. Plan the getaway before entering (vehicle placed, route chosen); the robbery itself is the easy half of each count.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape — one successful truck robbery with a clean getaway. Armored trucks are moving targets, so intercept rather than chase: block or disable the truck, take the money, and lose the wanted level to complete the 'escape' half of the description. A robbery that ends in arrest does not satisfy the text.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — the whole state, with no area total stated in the description, so this guide states none either. Exploration fills in as you travel for other trophies; the mop-up is driving or flying the districts you have never entered. Check the in-game map's uncovered areas rather than a guessed region count, and use the cited lists for any area the fog refuses to lift.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang — one per gang, every gang covered. The description gives no gang total, so none is claimed here; the cited lists name the gangs and their operations. Robbing the same gang twice does not advance this trophy: variety across gangs is the requirement, and gang operations also feed the 100% checklist, so none of the work is wasted.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — a place-and-action trophy: Ocean Beach, a cocktail, a view. The description does not name the bar or the exact spot, so this guide does not invent one; head to Ocean Beach, find where cocktails are served with a view, and use the cited guides for the confirmed trigger. The ellipsis in the name is PlayStation's own, kept as published.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a showroom vehicle out through the glass, the traditional way. The description names no specific showroom, so any vehicle showroom exit made by smashing out should satisfy it; a polite exit through the door is exactly what 'classic style' rules out. Expect a wanted level and plan the drive away.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — a bowling action at one named alley. The description's 'follow-through' points at completing a bowling throw there rather than merely visiting; play bowling at that alley and finish a game. It also counts toward trying every activity type, so combine it with Master of None.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.missable_reason: The description is partner-shaped ('a partnership') with no steps given: anything that depends on partner availability or a partner activity window is flagged rather than assumed permanent.
trophies.guide: The official description — 'A partnership with mass appeal' — gives no steps at all, and this guide will not invent a partner activity, a crowd size or a location to fill the gap. What the text supports is only this: a partnership is involved. The cited lists carry the confirmed trigger; until then, treat partner activities with an audience as the place to look, and bank it while partner free-roam is available.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missable_reason: The description counts choices made: story choices happen once and cannot be remade, so a counter fed by one-time decisions is flagged — play the story making choices deliberately instead of skipping them.
trophies.guide: Choices made, for better or worse — a counter fed by decisions taken during play. The description states no total, so none is claimed here; PlayStation tracks the progress target and the cited lists name it. Because story choices cannot be remade (missions do not replay), the practical advice is simple: engage with every choice the game offers instead of rushing past prompts, and keep manual saves before big story beats.

sources.name: Press Start — full trophy list, 18 Nov 2026

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missable_reason: The description is built on a second attempt: whatever it counts must be attempted once first, so skipping or avoiding the first attempt entirely is the failure mode — flagged so the first attempt is not dodged.
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm — the trophy is defined by a retry: something attempted once, then attempted again. The description does not name the activity, so this guide does not guess one; the cited lists carry the confirmed trigger. The actionable reading of the text alone: when something can be attempted again after a first try, take the second attempt instead of walking away.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: The official description — 'What the hell just happened?' — describes a reaction, not a task: something strange happens and the trophy marks witnessing it. No location, time or trigger can be honestly derived from that text, and none is invented here. The cited lists carry the confirmed event; treat any genuinely strange free-roam encounter as a candidate and check the sources for the exact one.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by — a melee attack delivered from a moving vehicle, bowling people over like pins. The description sets no count, so a single successful melee drive-by that connects should satisfy it; the name suggests a group, so aim for a cluster of targets rather than one pedestrian. Pair it with the bowling-alley trophy for thematic efficiency, if not for progress.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts — a money counter, tracked here in dollars with the stepper. Only laundered Marked Bills count, not general income, so route every batch of Marked Bills through contacts instead of letting them sit. It is a long counter: feed it steadily from stage 3 onward rather than grinding the full quarter-million at the end.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — cumulative shop spending, tracked here in dollars. 'Across all shops' means the total is what matters, not variety, though spreading purchases also helps the vehicle-discovery and property trophies. Buy useful things first (vehicles, property, gear for counted trophies) and let the counter fill as a by-product; only mop up the remainder with deliberate spending near the end.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties — every one, with no total stated in the description, so none is claimed here. Properties are a money sink, so sequence them after income trophies (laundering, robberies) and alongside the shop-spending counter, which property purchases feed. The cited lists name the properties and prices; buy as funds allow and finish the set in stage 4.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — ten registrations, tracked with the stepper. Register vehicles as you acquire or discover them (it pairs naturally with the 100-vehicle discovery trophy) instead of hunting ten registrable vehicles at the end. Only completed registrations count; if the app rejects a vehicle, move on to the next rather than forcing it.
